# S42 — TUI reordering and re-prioritizing are one step at a time

**Findings:** dogfooding; reorder at scale · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** a full drag interaction; discrete jumps cover the pain.

## Why

`J`/`K` move an item one position per keystroke, so dragging something from the bottom of a three-dozen-item queue to the top is dozens of presses. There is no move-to-top and no move-to-position in the TUI.

Re-prioritizing in the TUI is already possible — importance and urgency are editable with `e` — and `slicer sort` bulk-orders the whole queue by score from the CLI. This slice is now only the in-TUI reorder ergonomics.

## Files

- `src/slicer/tui.py` — move-to-top / move-to-position keys, score-set keys

## Failing tests

1. A move-to-top key puts the selected item first via `ops.move`.
2. A move-to-position prompt moves it there.
3. Setting importance/urgency from the TUI adjusts the score.

## Implement

Add move-to-top and move-to-position (prompting for a target) in the TUI, routed through `ops.move`, so a queue can be reordered in place without dropping to the CLI. Pure `act` paths as usual.

**Not in this slice:** re-prioritizing (done via `e` on importance/urgency) and bulk score-ordering (done by `slicer sort`).

## Check

Reordering and re-prioritizing a large queue takes a few keystrokes, not dozens.

One commit.
